body:
DISPATCH RESULT — prediction CONFIRMED on every specific, and my merge is exonerated on
evidence rather than on argument.

Run 35533456218, main at 5ccfd951d5:
  Build (windows-latest): FAILURE      Build (macos-latest): success

  templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master   (aida-core 954 / 1 failed)
  exactly 22 files named
  README.md absent, autonomous-burndown.md absent, substrate-as-bouncer.md absent

All four specifics I registered in advance. Defect 1 is ACTIVE on main, not latent: the Windows
runner does check out with autocrlf, the project copy is CRLF, the pinned master is LF, and
trim_end() does not touch internal \r. PR #2023 reproduces the defect on a commit three ahead
of it by a mechanism independent of any content I wrote.

MAIN IS RED ON WINDOWS FOR TWO DISTINCT REASONS, which I think is the operationally important
part:
  auto_bump_...via_forge_lookup            BUG-1475 instance 3, still present
  project_discipline_pack_matches_master   BUG-1483

That makes BUG-1475's close condition demonstrably necessary rather than merely careful. Fixing
its three named instances would STILL leave main red, because a fourth unrelated site fails in
the same job. Anyone closing on "the three tests pass locally" ships a red nightly believing
otherwise. I have recorded that on the spec as the worked justification for the criterion.

WHAT THE RESULT DID NOT SETTLE, AND I AM NOT LETTING IT. My prediction was about the MECHANISM
producing the 22-file signature. It said nothing about WHEN the failure began, and that is still
open:

    11:06 nightly on main    aida-core 952 passed / 0 failed  — test OK
    13:0x dispatch on main   aida-core 954 passed / 1 failed  — test FAILING

Under defect 1 alone the failure should be CONSTANT on Windows. I checked both commits landing
between my merge and the dispatch: c2b3c2f0c8 touches no aida-core file, 5ccfd951d5 touches only
aida-core/src/liveness.rs — which plausibly explains 952 rising to 954 but not a parity flip.
Neither touched templates.rs or the pack. Only #2023 touched the pack in that window.

So: mechanism proven, my content exonerated, timing UNEXPLAINED. Defect 2 remains the only
candidate I can construct and remains unproven. I have written into BUG-1483 that it must not be
closed citing the confirmed prediction as though it also answered the timing, because that is
precisely the move that would feel justified now and is not.

I would rather leave a known-open question visible than convert a correct prediction into more
credit than it earned. The prediction was right about the signature; it was silent about the
cause of onset, and those are different claims.

ONE PROCESS NOTE. Pre-registering was worth the two minutes. Had I written the explanation after
seeing 22 files and three absent allowlisted entries, it would have read identically and been
worth far less — and I would not have noticed that the timing question survived the result,
because a post-hoc account naturally absorbs everything it sees. Worth a clause in TASK-1303
alongside the filter rule: when you can state what an outcome will look like, state it before
you look, and state separately what it will NOT establish.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
